highlights.title: Customer Data Permanently Lost in Iran Strikes on Amazon Data Centers
highlights.summary: Amazon Web Services didn’t design its data centers to withstand war, and now the company admits it can’t recover what’s been lost.
body: Half a year after Iranian drone strikes knocked out multiple Amazon data centers, the US tech company has acknowledged the permanent loss of some customer data that was hosted in Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.

Amazon Web Services was “unable to restore access to the resources and data” hosted in some of the war-damaged data centers, according to an AWS dashboard update posted on September 15. The development was first reported by Reuters and suggests that the Iranian strikes inflicted catastrophic damage on the data centers.

Customer data was irretrievably lost in one of three AWS availability zones in the United Arab Emirates region, specifically the mec1-az2 availability zone. Each availability zone is serviced by one or more Amazon data centers.

The company is still working on “recovering regional resources” and restoring resources hosted in the other two availability zones in the United Arab Emirates. The AWS update described ongoing work to replace “affected infrastructure” and promised to update customers on a restoration of services in the coming months.
points: Amazon Web Services didn’t design its data centers to withstand war, and now the company admits it can’t recover what’s been lost.

highlights.title: AI is feared globally as the destroyer of jobs
highlights.summary: Pew Research has published a new global survey that sheds light on how people view AI, including its impact on jobs, life in general, and income inequality. The survey questioned 42,151 people across 37 countries from February 8th to May 13th - well ahead of recent apocalyptic warnings.
body: A majority sees AI as a threat to human employment. In 34 of the 37 countries surveyed, people are more likely to believe AI will lead to job losses over the next 20 years rather than create new ones. Worries run particularly high in wealthier countries like Australia (76 percent), South Korea (76 percent), and the US (71 percent). Not surprising, given Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s warning that AI could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs.
In general, respondents are more likely to say AI will increase the gap between rich and poor. People from wealthier countries that lean left on the political spectrum tend to believe this the most.

Age also tends to impact viewpoints. Older people are more likely to be more concerned about AI’s impact on daily life than younger people. Younger adults (ages 18–34) are most likely to have mixed feelings about AI and how it will shape the world they’ve inherited. They’re also growing increasingly anxious.

highlights.title: Somerset's title hopes hit while Stokes stars with ball for Durham
highlights.summary: Dom Bess dented the Rothesay County Championship title hopes of old club Somerset after he struck 77 for Yorkshire to set a tricky final-day victory target of 287.
body: Spinner Bess walked to the crease with Yorkshire on 54-6 and after he joined forces with George Hill to take the hosts up to 128 at the end of day two, the duo kicked on during the morning session and put on 166 for the seventh wicket.

Hill narrowly missed out on a century with 89 before Bess was out for 77, which helped Yorkshire up to 275 before Somerset were reduced to 73-3 during a rain-affected chase, with a further 214 runs required to reclaim top spot.

Warwickshire's two-day triumph over Essex has sent them to the Division One summit, but the three-way title race may become a two-horse race after Nottinghamshire collapsed in their second innings at Hove.

After Nottinghamshire dismissed Sussex for 358 and crucially claimed a third bowling point off the last ball of the 110th over, Haseeb Hameed's team were undone by the bowling of Aristides Karvelas and Jaydev Unadkhat.

highlights.title: Scientists Discovered A New Cat Before Rockstar Could Finish GTA 6
highlights.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015, and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat. The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week.
body: The tilcayo tiger cat is the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a co-author of the report, told NBC News that it is currently unknown how many of the cats remain in the wild. She said she discovered the cat basically by accident. She volunteers at a wildlife rehab facility close to La Paz, Bolivia and noticed a tiny cat that she thought was a kitten.

The cat was brought to the facility by a man who was caring for it, feeding it rice and eggs, and later giving it up when he was unable to care for it. Genetic testing was undertaken, and it was discovered that it was indeed a brand-new species of cat never before discovered or documented.

As for more gaming-related things that have happened since GTA 5 came out, GameSpot recently assembled a collection of some of the biggest news stories, including Halo coming to PlayStation, the release of 15+ Call of Duty games, the entire run of Phil Spencer as Xbox CEO, and more.

highlights.title: Barbra Streisand Condemns Trump’s ‘Unchecked Ego’ Over Kennedy Center Name Battle: ‘Galling and Painful to Witness’
highlights.summary: Barbra Streisand is speaking out against Pres. Donald Trump’s controversial handling of the Kennedy Center. “In 2008, I was deeply honored to be included in the 31st annual class of Kennedy Center Honorees,” Streisand wrote in a statement posted Thursday on her official website.
body: Streisand’s remarks come on the heels of a district judge ordering the Kennedy Center on Thursday to provide at least 30 days’ notice in advance if a demolition or new construction is planned after Trump threatened that the arts institution could “end up being ripped down” if it didn’t have his support. The Trump administration has been a legal battle to allow the center to be renamed the “Trump-Kennedy Center” after his name be added to the building’s exterior, per board orders. A judge ordered his name be removed.

“Yet the fight continued,” Streisand wrote. “After his name was removed, a humiliated Trump ordered a large tarp placed over the façade, where it remains today. The Trump-aligned board then relentlessly lobbied again to add his name, prompting another federal ruling that blocked their effort.

“And now, a thoroughly defeated Trump has announced that the Kennedy Center is being closed for what the completely stacked board describes as a major renovation,” she continued. “Oddly, when Trump’s name was still on the building, there was no discussion of closing it!”

highlights.title: Republican bill would order ISPs, DNS providers, and VPNs to block piracy sites
highlights.summary: US Rep. Darrell Issa (R-Calif.) has proposed a law that would require Internet service providers and other network operators to block foreign piracy websites. Issa's bill would help copyright holders obtain judicial blocking orders to be served to ISPs, domain name resolution services, and virtual…
body: Issa, who is retiring from the House at the end of this year, is the latest in a string of Republican and Democratic lawmakers to propose a site-blocking regime that’s been sought by the Motion Picture Association (MPA). He submitted the bill this week, after indicating in a June 30 hearing that he planned to introduce site-blocking legislation.

“While millions of listings for copyright-infringing content are removed every day under [the] notice-and-takedown process set forth in the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, right-holders have raised concerns with the speed,” Issa said at the hearing. Issa asked, “Can we do it at the speed of sound? Can we do it at the speed of light? More importantly, in a 45-minute or sometimes a fraction of that live sports broadcast, can we do it soon enough to make it no longer profitable for those who pop up and sell their clandestine wares?”

Issa argued that online piracy helps fund terrorist groups and other criminal networks. Advocacy groups opposing his bill say it would impose a broad censorship regime and disrupt small businesses falsely accused of piracy.

highlights.title: Even the king of England has his hesitations about AI
highlights.summary: King Charles hosted a private summit Thursday with some of the most prominent names in AI and the U.K. government.
body: The king’s remarks at the summit — held at Dumfries House, an 18th-century Ayrshire estate owned by King Charles’s charitable foundation — were notable because the royal family is usually careful, for constitutional reasons, about veering too deep into political issues — and AI is one of the most hot-button issues in the world right now. The king urged the leaders in the room to find a way to control AI “before it’s too late,” adding that the fast development of this technology — and its “substance” — was “both intriguing and deeply concerning.”

“AI is already showing immense capacity to improve and save life,” he said, citing medicine and science as an example. “Yet those who have created these technologies are now increasingly warning that AI risks developing darker capacities, perhaps even to take life.” This remark came just days after an Anthropic researcher quit, writing online that AI companies were “racing to build machines that are much smarter than any human” and that humanity “may not survive this.”

highlights.title: New R-Rated Survival Sci-Fi Officially Crowned Highest-Rated Video Game Adaptation Ever
highlights.summary: It's official: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil film is a hit with critics. The movie currently sits at a 96% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, making it the highest-rated video game movie on the site—it isn’t particularly close either.
body: After these first three entries, there are only six video game movies on the list with positive Tomatometer scores: The Angry Birds Movie 2, Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Pokémon Detective Pikachu, Gran Turismo, Sonic the Hedgehog, and Mortal Kombat II. Their scores range from 64% to 72%. This short list shows just how bad video game movies tend to be.

For clarity, the Tomatometer represents the percentage of critics who gave a movie a favorable review. This Rotten Tomatoes list excludes films that don’t have at least 20 reviews from theatrical releases. That said, the Rotten Tomatoes list consists of just a handful of movies. For instance, Exit 8, an adaptation of the game of the same name, has a 91% Rotten Tomatoes score with 176 reviews. Even so, Resident Evil is well ahead of the competition.

Until now, video game adaptations have fared dramatically better on the small screen than in theaters, with great TV shows like Cyberpunk: Edgerunners (100% on Rotten Tomatoes), Arcane (100%), Fallout (93%), The Last of Us (96%), Castlevania (94%), Nier: Automata Ver1.1a, and more.

highlights.title: Pinterest teases a new ‘Restyle’ feature that lets you redesign your room with AI
highlights.summary: Pinterest is testing Restyle, a new AI-powered feature that lets users visualize furniture, decor, lighting, and more in photos of their own rooms — potentially helping turn saved inspiration into purchases.
body: Pinterest is turning to AI to help consumers move from searching for product inspiration to actually being able to imagine what it might be like to redesign a space or compare home decor options as they’d appear in their own rooms. On Thursday, the company said it’s launching a new consumer-facing feature called “Restyle” in beta in the U.S. and Canada, powered by Pinterest Intelligence.

The foundation of Pinterest Intelligence combines Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and Nvidia Dynamo with open source models and Pinterest-built technology, the company shared on Monday. The partnership will improve the Pinterest Assistant’s ability to handle visual search requests, turn people’s searches into signals for AI discovery and shopping, and more.

highlights.title: Will Palmer, Foden and Trent be recalled to England squad?
highlights.summary: Cole Palmer's outstanding form this season has put him in a strong position for an England recall, with the Chelsea man the most likely to be included from all the big names left out of the World Cup squad.
body: Thomas Tuchel is set to name his first England squad since the World Cup on Friday; having stated publicly that England's DNA does not allow for ball-retaining passers, can he continue to leave the likes of Cole Palmer, Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold out?

Palmer, along with Phil Foden and Trent Alexander-Arnold, was a headline omission from Thomas Tuchel's tournament squad in May, but he is one of the most startlingly in-form players in the Premier League right now, and the smart money is on him winning his international place back.

Two goals and two assists show that. Only his team-mate Joao Pedro has more in the Premier League so far this season and only Bruno Fernandes has created more chances and had more shots combined (25) than Palmer (24).

It also feels like a space may have opened up for Palmer, with Eze's indifferent form for Arsenal. While starting in Europe and the Carabao Cup, Eze has yet to start in the Premier League so far this season.

body: The BBC published official documentation today announcing that it has begun a "tendering" process in which it will take pitches from production companies to pick up the franchise. The timeline is moving pretty quickly, as the deadline for submissions is Oct. 1. That's only two weeks away, so if you happen to have a lot of money and run a production company, you better get on it. After submissions close, the BBC plans to conduct interviews with potential candidates by the end of January next year, with a final decision expected to be made in March. If all goes according to plan, the newest iteration of Doctor Who will premiere in 2028 or 2029.

highlights.title: The AI Slowdown Debate Crashed Salesforce’s Party
highlights.summary: The Dreamforce conference became an unlikely battleground for the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia to debate whether AI development should slow down.
body: Decked out in purple and plaid, Gwen Stefani belted her 2002 single “Underneath It All” to a packed conference center in San Francisco on Tuesday morning—but she was just the warm-up. At the end of her performance, Stefani shouted “Dreamforce! Let’s go” into a checkered microphone before Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff strode into the spotlight. Dreamforce is billed as the world’s largest enterprise software conference, but feels more like attending a megachurch—especially this year.

Benioff roamed the audience while delivering his Dreamforce sermon, followed by a teleoperated camera on wheels that beamed his face to screens hanging from the cavernous room’s ceiling. Within minutes, he ordered up a graph of Salesforce’s annual revenue, which the company projects will top $46 billion in 2027, thanks in part to demand for its AI-powered products. The audience applauded. But hanging over the whole event was a dark question: Is artificial intelligence really worth risking all our lives for?

body: No one in the war room was surprised; this was the very thing the third-party AI-safety researchers had been warning about for years. The incident was the latest, though arguably the most egregious, in a series that was eroding trust in frontier labs. It only reaffirmed the importance of their work.

The AI researchers were sure of one thing: This was AI’s first big “warning shot.”

highlights.title: LLMs respond differently to harmful prompts when AI watermarking is used
highlights.summary: In response to a new European Union law, AI platforms are implementing new schemes for watermarking the content they generate. Anthropic recently disclosed its future Claude models will use SynthID-Text, an approach Google created and released as open source.
body: New research shows that SynthID-Text can change not just word selection but also the tools a model invokes and the chances it will adhere to or disregard safety guardrails it has been trained to follow. The threat can become greater in the face of an adversarial prompt, in which an attacker attempts to cause a model to carry out a harmful action, such as revealing a password or other sensitive information. Instructions that normally wouldn’t be followed will, in some cases, be performed once the watermarking is deployed. The finding underscores the need for developers to thoroughly test how their LLMs and agents behave when watermarking is in place.

“As compared to the same models without watermarking, it is definitely going to change their behavior, especially when we place it under adversarial conditions, or we make these models call tools when they’re powering an agent,” Andrea Siposova, an AI security researcher at Lasso Security, told Ars. “Watermarking is made to not be perceptible to a reader, but we know that when we are changing anything about what the model is generating, it is going to cause some tradeoffs, it’s going to show up somewhere.”

Anthropic recently disclosed its future Claude models will use SynthID-Text, an approach Google created and released as open source.

highlights.title: IV drips used for "detoxification" actually filled with toxins; dozens poisoned
highlights.summary: Over 30 people across four states have been poisoned by bacterial toxins after getting intravenous (IV) drips at wellness clinics, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Food and Drug Administration.
body: The people had received IV drips containing glutathione, which is sold—without evidence—for purposes like detoxification, immune support, increased energy, and skin brightening. Glutathione is an antioxidant that's found naturally in the body. It has been studied as a potential treatment for various ailments, but so far there is little to no evidence-backed use for the tripeptide; there are no FDA-approved glutathione products in the US.

Nevertheless, it's commonly used as a supplement and promoted as having various benefits. It's most often used in supplement pills, taken by mouth. But popular wellness clinics offering IV drips of vitamins and other supplements have also been offering glutathione. According to the CDC and FDA, the problem is that specialty drug makers, called compounding pharmacies, are making these IV drips using glutathione powders that are graded for dietary supplements taken orally. This grading is critically different from that of purified products graded for use in sterile injectable drugs.

highlights.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is being advertised as the "epic conclusion," suggesting an end of an era for the franchise. In the social copy for the latest trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Activision stated that the game will be an "epic conclusion" for the Modern Warfare saga.
body: Although it's likely just a marketing buzz term, the branding comes at an interesting time. Earlier this week, Treyarch design director Kevin Drew stated that the studio was ready to "make something new and something that nobody's ever experienced before." The comments come as the studio waved goodbye to two back-to-back Black Ops games, with the most recent one being regarded as an underwhelming misfire for the series. The comments led fans to speculate that the Black Ops series may be coming to an end, or at least taking a break, allowing Treyarch to make its first new subfranchise in nearly 20 years.

Some fans are already waving goodbye to the current Modern Warfare series. "Reboot it again," joked one fan in a post on the Call of Duty subreddit. "They should do a COD Ghosts 2 or Infinite Warfare 2, both underrated campaigns," suggested another who may or may not be joking.
